structuredContent.title: Kinetic identity field
structuredContent.description: Original Pulse, Weave and Orbit formations with stable object identity, multiple continuous spring channels, elapsed phase and reduced-motion poses. Consumer owns SVG/Three geometry and lighting.

sources.source:
# Evidence for creation and refinement

Before capture, write the actual product journey and its positive result, deadlines, error states and interruption cases. Example for a colony launch page: open the task panel, select a worker, switch worker while its token is traveling, run the task, and verify that the visible result corresponds to the selected worker. Verify the ordinary CTA and links independently. A looping ant scene is not task completion.

Capture a trusted credential-free local development page at desktop and narrow widths. Use a unique target and the same viewport, interactions, duration, reduced-motion preference and explicit contracts across before/after runs. Include the delayed end, not only the initial reveal. Keep enough frames around reversals and final state. The tool returns a capture ID and stores real browser footage; do not synthesize traces or substitute scene counters for measurements.

1. `motion_capture({recipe})` records the specified interaction.
2. `motion_inspect({captureId,fromMs,toMs,includeSamples:true})` reveals the event/sample context around a finding.
3. `motion_frames({captureId,timestampsMs})` returns recorded native images; look at them, including intermediate states.
4. After a source repair, rerun the unchanged recipe and use `motion_compare({beforeId,afterId})`; inspect the after frames as well.

Obtain tool schema and current limits from the connected server; do not invent arguments or shorten a journey to fit the default capture duration. Each wait is at most 4000ms, all waits total at most 10000ms, and the entire interaction is at most 12000ms. Leave room for actual clicks and settling. `contract.outcomes.timeoutMs` is a deadline measured from capture START, including actions; it is not an extra timeout after the final wait. Omit it to use the capture duration. Positive checks run after the actions before that deadline; forbidden visible errors are observed throughout. For example, use a 12000ms capture with three waits of 3000ms for a nine-second task, with no shorter outcome timeout.

The ordinary browser remains available for outcome assertions, keyboard journeys, screenshots and long interactions. Capture tools are observation tools; the host coding agent writes source and tests. Do not loosen budgets after seeing a failure.

The interaction deadline also applies to exploratory captures without outcomes. Overlong waits or blocked inputs retain incomplete evidence rather than a completed report. `recipeWarnings` identifies known wait/drag schedules that exhaust the budget; leave additional room for real input. For held scrubbing, use `action:"drag"`, a unique selector, 2–12 normalized `{x,y}` waypoints and 100–2000ms duration. Every reversal is visited while the native pointer stays down, then it is released even on failure. Match the recorded range to its actual thumb geometry; observe release state separately from any playback that resumes afterward.

Canvas movement needs footage of the canvas contents. A static DOM box can contain rich motion or a stalled renderer. Frame cadence, motion continuity, meaningful final state and visual composition are separate observations. Static screenshots cannot establish smoothness; sparse frames and dropped/insufficient footage are inconclusive. Report the exact source revision, runtime, viewport, captures and checks. Distinguish protocol/tool connectivity from an actual fresh agent-host invocation.

For a matched A/B, preserve the same brief, model, assets and comparable effort; both agents retain ordinary browser tools. Log the extra plugin guidance and tool use in the assisted condition. Preserve failures and incomplete recordings. A recipe demonstration or handwritten repair proves the artifact behaves as inspected; it does not establish general coding-agent improvement.

# Constrained transition authoring

The runtime schema is `transitionPlanSchema` exported by Motion Debugger. Serialize `schemaVersion: 1`, an explicit `browser-monotonic-ms` or `controlled-preview-ms` clock, stable logical actor IDs, DOM/SVG selectors or owned Three object/camera IDs, source locations and protected visual attributes. Projected screen positions use CSS pixels; orientation uses radians. World/parent positions use declared scene units and must be projected before pixel acceptance checks. Every beat has a trigger, purpose, from/to pose, acyclic `after` dependencies, duration and overlap. App states can still cycle open/close/reopen.

`inputPolicy` declares latest-input wins. Retargeting carries position and velocity. Direct scrub and intentional cuts carry none and exclude continuity checks. Acceptance includes useful completion, forbidden visible errors, reduced motion and per-actor destination tolerances, response/settling bounds and required travel. A stationary canvas is not actor evidence. Save permitted source files, protected files and bounded editable parameter names with the plan.

Use `createDOMBinding`, `createSVGBinding` or `createThreeBinding` on original objects. Resolve relative DOM positions with `begin()` at transition start. Invalidate on viewport/layout/scene changes and rebind before advancing. Three bindings own no renderer, camera or geometry; they write parent-local transforms in the existing render loop. Consumers explicitly project world destinations and supply custom material mappings when needed.

`createPersistentHandoff` retargets the existing spring channels without resets. `createStagedDecomposition` accepts editable beat targets and relative phase overlap. `createDragReleaseSettling` distinguishes direct pointer seeking from release retargeting. Advance controllers using native elapsed seconds from the consumer's existing renderer. Initialize the elapsed clock from the first native frame callback (zero initial delta); an earlier frame timestamp can precede performance.now() read during module setup. If the consumer stops its render loop while paused, reset that elapsed baseline when resuming so paused wall time is not integrated. All retain pause, replay and meaningful reduced-motion targets. Dispose controllers without disposing consumer objects.

Before normal coding edits, call `snapshotProtectedDesign(projectRoot, plan.edits.protectedFiles)` or freeze equivalent exact SHA-256 hashes. Verify these bytes after every candidate. Protect assets, layout, copy, materials and interactions unless explicitly permitted. Keep the current candidate, one minimal revision and optional alternative staging: at most three total under the same budget. Rendering, reviews, tool calls, decoding and failed attempts all count.

Execute the same short native journey and meaningful contracts for each candidate. Reject failed/unverified function or changed protected design first. Keep motion meaning, response, trackability and visual preference as separate judgments; cite actual delivered native capture/event/frame evidence. `selectMotionCandidate` validates bounds, measured costs and citation correspondence; it is a nomination guard, not an aesthetic oracle or proof that a model perceived the frames. Critic nominations may abstain and require calibration against blinded humans before serving as the main selector. Pose previews cannot support timing/performance claims.

Create a recoverable `createVerifiedMotionCheckpoint` only for a functional native-verified candidate with unchanged protected hashes. It retains exact authorized source bytes, plan/bindings, evidence IDs and hashes. Restore through normal host editing tools if later revisions fail. Retain every attempt and stop within the existing two-repair bound. Save successful app-specific configurations and regression journeys, with why they helped and which constraints passed.
